spans.text: M200 kicks open the door to the safe house.
I've successfully linked up with the hostage!
You're here at last!
This is Gr SL8, I'm in good condition, ready to join the battle at any time.
Let's talk on the move!
We managed to shake off the Uhlans, but the Gladiators and an Isomer are still on our backs. Things aren't looking good!
Right, so where are the others?
They're fighting hit-and-run battles with the Gladiators.
Let's go back and help them.
VHS said we should first...
There are enemies up ahead.
We can't escape them with just the two of us.
While they debate, the Dolls suddenly feel their thought processes slowing down.
Click, click, click... The sound of high heels draws close.
Glassy-eyed Nytos move past them into the distance, while a run-down White Faction mech lunges at them with no sound or warning of its presence, ripping apart everything it touches.
Signals lost from all five Dolls.
Combat Simulation No. 8. Time elapsed - 18 minutes. System grading - B.
The fact that they could reach the hostage so quickly shows that Squad Puzzle has the ability to complete the training program.
Pause it for now. Let them do another post-op review.
Just as I'm about to say something to the gathered Dolls, I feel a hand gently touch my shoulder.
I'm very sorry to disturb you, Commander, but something urgent has come up.
No problem, go ahead.
I think I'll let Mr. Kryuger explain the specifics to you.
...Got it.
I sigh helplessly, then look one last time at the assembled squad before leaving with Helian.
...In Kryuger's office.
Coming here again after so long gives me a pang of nostalgia. It took me right back to when I first arrived at the Griffin base.
Right now, that imposing figure whose rock-solid presence is always infinitely reassuring is raising a wineglass to me.
Care for a drink, Commander?
...I thought you weren't the sort to drink on the job.
Indeed, but today is a bit of a special case.
Not going to help yourself?
Kryuger raises a bottle, and pours some clear liqour into the transparent glass.
In that case, don't mind if I do.
I take a seat in front of him and pick up the wineglass.
It's been a while since I had the chance to chat with you like this.
Looks like things have been quite peaceful for us recently.
I've long missed days like these.
Heh, only older people talk that way.
Well, getting sent on so many harrowing missions does tend to age you.
It seems that both your combat performance and your ability to gripe to your superiors are second to none.
Pardon me, I'll be more subtle next time.
I chuckle quietly, and Kryuger snorts in laughter too.
I honestly didn't expect you to come back alive from Paldiski.
Neither did a lot of people.
The raging flames, skin charred black by high temperatures, the bodies of fallen Dolls strewn across the ground, Kalina's eyes filled with despair...
I downed my glass of liquor in one gulp.
The burning sensation as it goes down reminds me of that day.
If there's anything you want to say, you can go ahead and tell me.
Your original mission was only to contain Sangvis Ferri.
However, the Sangvis Ferri forces which have plagued us for so long are little more than ants in the face of the Military and Paradeus.
Those enemies were not originally meant for you to handle, and yet you took care of them anyway.
You have done very well, so well that you have far exceeded our expectations.
Thank you for your praise.
Though I sense a "but" coming.
Indeed... But the Mastermind of Sangvis Ferri vanished in that base, along with M4 and M16.
And while the threat of the Military has been neutralized for now, the people who backed them are still hidden in the shadows.
I know you have worked very hard, but from a broader perspective, all we have done is little more than scratching an itch.
So, are we going to root out the one who's behind everything?
We need to choose an appropriate candidate for the task, because the situation we are about to face will be more complicated than ever.
I'm listening.
I was once a soldier myself, so I only trust people who have come back alive from the battlefield.
And there are only three kinds of people who come back from the battlefield.
The first kind are timid to the end of their days, who view even the daylight streaming into their rooms as an enemy bombardment.
The second are drunk on slaughter and bloodshed, who build their joy on the suffering of others.
You, Commander, belong to the third kind.
...The third kind?
They are people who know why they fight.
Their convictions make them keener, braver, fiercer, and more eager for battle.
...I just want to protect what I can protect. That's all.
You seek peace, and you fight for a better peace.
I understand that reasoning, and I also understand that what I can do is very limited.
And yet, you will not back down. You will not abandon any chance you have to fulfil your objective.
Sounds like you're hinting at a new mission.
So...you have a new lead?
Angelia works quickly and precisely.
There is a reason why Zelinsky favors her.
If you're talking about her investigation in Bremen... I know a little about it.
But I haven't been able to contact her ever since she left the refugee settlement.
You don't need to worry about her for now, Commander.
Also, I don't think you're content to always be trailing in her wake.
Sometimes, you need to learn how to overtake people.
Are you going to send me to Germany?
My hand freezes as I'm putting down my glass. I stare blankly at Kryuger until he nods in affirmation.
Like I just said, your valiant deeds at Paldiski have reached the ears of many.
Kryuger hands me an envelope.
A wax seal?
The document is so exquisite I can't help but gawk. To my knowledge, Kryuger has never been one for this sort of thing.
In the middle of the bright red wax seal is a vigorous griffin baring its claws, like a fearless challenger.
...A Griffin? Isn't this our logo?
Do you remember the full name of our company?
The company name?
..."Griffin and Kryuger".
Kryuger raises his glass and downs its contents in one mouthful.
We all call him the "Earl".
So should you.
I gulp and reach out to open the letter.
Kryuger raises a hand to stop me.
Read it on the plane.
...Got it.
When am I leaving?
Right now.
Right now? But...Kalina's still in hospital.
And the Dolls at the base aren't fully—
I know that this is not a good time.
...But it can't be helped, can it?
Bring the Dolls from Paldiski. They're more capable than we give them credit for.
Also, that Isomer that's connected to OGAS—I won't ask too many questions about her, but I
suggest
you bring her with you.
Is that really just a suggestion?
The frontline won't wait for you, Commander.
Head out as soon as possible.
Behind my back, my hand unconsciously feels for the holster at my waist. The familiar sensation reminds me that the pistol which Kryuger gave me is still there.
Understood, Mr. Kryuger.
Kryuger falls silent again. He refills his glass, but does not drink just yet.
Instead he swirls his glass, watching as the waves rise and fall in the colorless liquid within.
...Mr. Kryuger?
...This is probably unfair to you.
But all great endeavors demand sacrifice.
You gave me a choice.
And I chose.
Kryuger's mouth curls up in a smile, and he touches his glass to the table.
A tremor runs through my heart.
He is offering me a toast.
I briefly hesitate, then return his gaze steadily.
I raise my glass, and down it all in one go as he watches.
You will live until the end. I can sense it.
But I must give you a word of advice.
...Trust no one.
Does that include...yourself and "the Earl"?
Oh yes. ESPECIALLY him.
...At the Griffin base, in the heliport holding area.
The AR Team has already assembled by the time I get there.
Commander! What's this mission about?
It's a kind we've never taken on before.
Huh? Could it be...
I lay the pictures of the objective on the holding area table.
Why is it a girl?
...What is this?
Are we supposed to investigate her or protect her?
Neither.
Our mission is to proceed to Bohnsdorf, near Berlin, find our target, and bring her to a designated location.
We're going to kidnap a girl, then? We certainly haven't done anything like that before.
Someone will come to pick us up once we acquire the mission objective.
Tsk, isn't that what they say for every mission? We always end up having to make do on our own anyway.
This is our mission, so what is SHE doing here?
You have your mission, and I have answers of my own that I wish to find.
This mission is closely linked to Paradeus. Dandelion may end up being very helpful.
Dandelion stands behind the AR Team, ignoring ST AR-15's icy glare.
I smile weakly, and the communicator just happens to ring at that moment.
One second.
Understood.
I head to one side and look at my communicator. It's the latest report on Kalina's status from the hospital where she's admitted.
I quickly skim through it, until one sentence at the end captures my attention.
"Suspected mild symptoms of Eurosky Low-Emission Infectious Disease. Further verification in progress."
My finger trembles as I tap out a phone number.
(Dial tone)
Hi! This is Kalina!
Ka...
Sorry, but I can't come to the phone right now.
If it's urgent, please contact Miss Helian; if it's about something else, please leave your message after the beep.
Beep—
Wait for me.
The plane has finished its pre-flight checks, and we can board anytime.
I end the call and head toward the AR Team.
The sky today is a bright, clear blue.
